And to say that him breaking his neck is worse:

Because breaking your bones and bleeding internally, things that occur from being thrown into a wall at high velocity and then falling down a long way, while simultaneously being exposed to sub-zero temperatures is a slow and horrible way to die. This is Superman II. So WTF are people on about?
Wait.. I just rewatched Superman II... and Superman kills Zod? Am I missing something here? Not only that, the way he does it is a lot worse then the neck snapping BS.

The general thrust of the argument is that David S Goyer doesn't like and doesn't "get" Superman. So he wrote a bunch of ideas out that don't explore Supes very well. It's not just the badly conceived fight scenes, it's also the weird morality of the Kents, the weak/on the nose space- Jesus stuff, the apparent inclusion of many of Jon Peters' notorious Superman-looks-like-a-fag ideas (search out Kevin Smith's youtube video for the rundown on that). The self-seriousness of the whole thing. The mangled non-linear structure (not well handled - kept Clark at arms length from the audience). The utter tedium of buildings getting endlessly knocked over. The utterly fucked decision by Zack Snyder to not use his signature speed racking during a fight that actually would have benefited from it.

There's good stuff in there but it's badly written and structured and Snyder dropped a stylistic mechanism that would have helped the storytelling in favor of a shitty fake shaky cam technique.

Honestly I cared more about Zod and Jor El when they were on screen that the home team. I just felt numb when they were wrecking the fuck out of Metropolis, but found the bizarre high fantasy of Jor El riding an alien pterodactyl and fightin'-round-the-world on Krypton far more enjoyable than anything earthbound (and I'm not even a Russel Crowe fan). Supes as they present him in MoS does kinda need Batman to kick his ass to bitch slap him back to some kind of relateability and clear away all that martyr-complex they loaded him down with. Fanboys HATED Emo Peter Parker, but he was infinitely more fun than Emo Clark Kent.

I liked that Superman was distant and hard to actually feel connected with. It worked to the movie's strength that Superman isn't human and you're not supposed to see him as a super human, but an alien who looks human and will have different emotional structures.

Man of Steel is the only version of Superman I've liked because it felt far more in touch with reality to me. Yes the big lasers are dumb, but the actual fights felt grounded in reality. When you're powerful enough to go toe to toe with Superman, you're not going to fly to the Moon to fight him, you're going to fight him among as many people as possible so you force him to hesitate and gain an advantage. To me, this was an interesting Superman movie because I don't like the traditional usage of Superman, he is far too powerful to be interesting to me, same way Batman has far too many resources to ever be interesting.

There is room for classic Superman but also exploring the concept of Superman in new ways. Same way there is room for Adam West and Gravel throat as Batman.
